python -m senai.memory --project PROJECT --scope SCOPE [--user-id ID] profile-propose NAME TEXT [--origin human|outcome] [--verified]
python -m senai.memory --project PROJECT --scope SCOPE [--user-id ID] profile-apply PROPOSAL_JSON --approve
python -m senai.memory --project PROJECT --scope SCOPE [--user-id ID] session-context REQUEST [--include-user] [--max-chars N]

inputs: existing build_prompt output plus bounded snapshot
outputs: executor result unchanged; exceptions propagate; no implicit retention

storage.namespace: Recommended: canonical installation + fixed installation scope, one user across projects. Legacy explicit project/scope still supported.
storage.migration_notes: New flat SOUL.md/USER.md/MEMORY.md at INSTALLATION/outputs/.senai-memory alongside memory.db. Schema v1 unchanged, no silent copying/deletion/import of old scopes or hashed files.

shared_file_changes: Supersedes earlier multi-user proposal: configure one explicit installation root and use InstallationMemory.snapshot for fresh sessions across projects
Coordinator wires user-request/noteworthy/verified judgments into InstallationMemory.remember; SOUL remains human-only
Keep snapshot reuse on resume and native session behavior; shared CLI routing remains proposed; see integration-notes.md

limitations: Installation-wide mode assumes exactly one owner; not suitable for independent users sharing an installation
Shared configuration/CLI/native lifecycle and app noteworthy-event judgment are not wired or live tested
Decision flags are trusted caller assertions, not authorization or verification by the memory module
Legacy scoped data is preserved but not automatically migrated or loaded
Files remain bounded, frozen snapshots do not update mid-session; no automatic compaction/semantic deduplication
WSL/POSIX fcntl required; no new dependencies; unencrypted local data and incomplete credential pattern filters
Concurrent edits raise conflicts; no secure erasure or retraction of old session context
